author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A new national maternal-health report is prompting questions about how consistently Rhode Island families receive support from pregnancy through the postpartum period. The Harris Poll and digital maternal-health company Babyscripts focused on whether patients feel heard, can obtain help and remain connected to care after delivery.

RINewsToday used the findings to examine gaps that can persist even when a patient asks for assistance. The report emphasizes continuity across the full maternal-care timeline, rather than treating childbirth as the end of routine support. It also highlights the importance of clear follow-up, accessible treatment pathways and communication between patients and clinicians.

The findings do not provide a Rhode Island-specific performance score, but they offer practical questions for the state’s hospitals, insurers and public-health agencies. Those include how quickly postpartum concerns are assessed, whether referrals lead to actual appointments and how families are supported between scheduled visits. The local relevance is especially clear for mental-health concerns, which may emerge or intensify after a family leaves the hospital. The report’s central message is that asking for help should begin a reliable care process, not leave patients to navigate disconnected services alone.
dek: A Harris Poll and Babyscripts report is prompting local questions about follow-up, access and continuity after childbirth.
headline: Maternal-care report highlights postpartum support gaps for Rhode Island
